items.text: Products: $X,Y$ separable over $k$ $\Rightarrow$ $X\times_k Y$ separable ($(X\times Y)\times Z=X\times(Y\times Z)$ reduced for $Z$ reduced); likewise geometrically irreducible.
Geometrically integral

For a field $k$ equivalent: (a) $k$ algebraically closed; (b) $A,B$ integral domains $\Rightarrow$ $A\otimes_kB$ integral domain; (c) $A$ integral $\Rightarrow$ $A_{k'}$ integral for every extension $k'$; (d) $k'\otimes_k k'$ a domain for every finite extension $k'$.

$X$ over $k$, $K_1$ algebraically closed extension. Equivalent: (a) $X\times_k Y$ integral for all integral $Y$; (b) $X_{k'}$ integral for all $k'$; (c) $X_{K_1}$ integral; (d) $X_{k'}$ integral for finite $k'$.
Geometrically integral = separable and geometrically irreducible. Implies integral; converse for all $X$ iff $k$ is algebraically closed. Stable under $k'/k$ and products.
Connectedness
Theorem. $k$ separably closed, $X,Y$ connected over $k$ $\Rightarrow$ $X\times_k Y$ connected.
$\bar k/k$ radicial $\Rightarrow$ $\bar X=X_{\bar k}\to X$ is a homeomorphism; so topological statements for $k$ separably closed reduce to $k$ algebraically closed.
First proof, $X,Y$ locally of finite type (so locally noetherian): join $z,z'$ by chains of irreducible components.

General proof
Admitted (flat descent): $X\times_kY\to X$ is surjective and open, so $X$ has the quotient topology.
Step 1: $X$ connected non-empty $\Rightarrow$ $X_{k'}$ connected, for every extension $k'$.
A surjection onto a quotient space with connected fibres, from a space whose target is connected, has connected source (open-closed subsets are saturated).
\text{fibre over }x:\ \operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\kappa(x)\otimes_kk'\bigr),\ \ \text{irreducible since }k\ \text{is separably closed, hence connected}
\text{General }Y:\quad X\times_kY\to Y,\ \ \text{fibre at }y\ \text{is}\ X_{\kappa(y)}\ \text{(connected, non-empty)}

Sharpness: $\operatorname{Spec}k'\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k'=\coprod_{\Gamma}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ for $k'/k$ finite Galois with group $\Gamma$; connected only if $\Gamma=1$, so $k$ separably closed is necessary.
Geometrically connected
$X$ over $k$, $K_1$ a separably closed extension. Equivalent: (a) $X\times_kY$ connected for all connected $Y$; (b) $X_{k'}$ connected for all $k'$;
(c) $X_{K_1}$ connected; (d) $X_{k'}$ connected for every finite Galois $k'/k$. Then $X$ is geometrically connected, which implies connected; the converse for all $X$ iff $k$ separably closed.
(b)$\Rightarrow$(a): $X\times_kY\to Y$ surjective with connected fibres $X_{\kappa(y)}$, and $Y$ has the quotient topology.
(c)$\Rightarrow$(b): $X_{k'}$ is the image of the connected $X_{K_1'}$.
(d)\Rightarrow(c):\ K_1=\varinjlim k_i\ \text{(finite Galois)},\qquad X_{K_1}=\varprojlim X_{k_i}\ \text{(affine over }X),\quad X\ \text{quasi-compact}
An open-closed subset of the limit comes from an open-closed subset of $X_{k_i}$ for $i$ large, which is empty or everything since $X_{k_i}$ is connected.
$X$ geometrically connected over $k$ $\iff$ $X_{k'}$ over $k'$; products of geometrically connected schemes are geometrically connected.
